questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Green Revolution' in India was primarily associated with increased production of which crops?
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution (1960s-70s) led by M.S. Swaminathan focused on high-yielding varieties of wheat and rice, dramatically increasing their production. Sugarcane and Cotton are commercial crops not central to the Green Revolution. Pulses and Oilseeds were largely bypassed by it. Tea and Coffee are plantation crops unrelated to this movement.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013:

(i) It provides subsidized food grains to approximately two-thirds of India's population.
(ii) Under the Act, rice is provided at ₹3 per kg, wheat at ₹2 per kg, and coarse grains at ₹1 per kg.
(iii) The Act identifies beneficiaries under Priority Households and Antyodaya Anna Yojana categories.
(iv) It is implemented exclusively by the Central Government without state involvement.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — NFSA covers about 67% of the population (75% rural, 50% urban). Statement (ii) is correct — the subsidized prices are ₹3/₹2/₹1 per kg for rice/wheat/coarse grains. Statement (iii) is correct — beneficiaries are categorized as Priority Households and AAY. Statement (iv) is incorrect — implementation involves both Centre and States; states identify beneficiaries and run the Public Distribution System.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India is the world's largest producer of milk.
Reason (R): Operation Flood, launched by Dr. Verghese Kurien, revolutionized dairy farming in India through cooperative models.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — India is the world's largest milk producer (over 230 million tonnes annually). Reason (R) is correct — Operation Flood (White Revolution), spearheaded by Dr. Verghese Kurien through NDDB and the Amul cooperative model, transformed India from a milk-deficient nation to the world's largest producer. The Reason directly explains how India achieved the status in (A). Option B is wrong because (R) is the direct cause of (A). Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following revolutions in Indian agriculture with their associated products:

Column I:
(a) White Revolution
(b) Blue Revolution
(c) Yellow Revolution
(d) Golden Revolution

Column II:
(i) Oilseeds
(ii) Horticulture (fruits/honey)
(iii) Fish/Aquaculture
(iv) Milk/Dairy

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: White Revolution relates to milk/dairy production (a-iv). Blue Revolution relates to fish and aquaculture (b-iii). Yellow Revolution relates to oilseeds production (c-i). Golden Revolution relates to horticulture including fruits and honey (d-ii). Option B swaps White with Blue. Option C swaps Blue with Yellow. Option D mismatches White with horticulture.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are objectives of the 'Make in India' initiative?

(i) Promote manufacturing in India
(ii) Attract foreign direct investment
(iii) Create employment opportunities
(iv) Discourage imports of all goods

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Make in India (launched 2014) aims to promote manufacturing (i), attract FDI (ii), and create employment (iii). Statement (iv) is incorrect — the initiative does not aim to discourage ALL imports; it seeks to boost domestic manufacturing capacity and self-reliance in key sectors, not impose blanket import restrictions.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Minimum Support Price (MSP) for crops in India is announced by:
options: Government of India on the recommendation of CACP
questions.correctAnswer: Government of India on the recommendation of CACP
questions.explanation: MSP is announced by the Central Government based on recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP). RBI deals with monetary policy, not agricultural pricing. NABARD is a development bank for agriculture but doesn't fix MSP. State Governments do not independently set MSP — it is a Central Government function.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about India's industrial policy:

(i) The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 classified industries into three categories.
(ii) Liberalization in 1991 abolished the 'License Raj' for most industries.
(iii) The public sector was given the leading role in industrial development in 1956.
(iv) After 1991, FDI was completely prohibited in all sectors.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — the 1956 policy divided industries into Schedule A (state monopoly), Schedule B (mixed), and Schedule C (private). Statement (ii) is correct — the 1991 reforms dismantled the License Raj. Statement (iii) is correct — the 1956 resolution gave the public sector a commanding role. Statement (iv) is incorrect — 1991 OPENED India to FDI rather than prohibiting it.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'PM-KISAN' scheme provides:
options: ₹6,000 per year in three instalments to eligible farmer families
Loan waiver for all agricultural debts
Free irrigation facility to small farmers
questions.correctAnswer: ₹6,000 per year in three instalments to eligible farmer families
questions.explanation: PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi) provides ₹6,000 per year in three equal instalments of ₹2,000 each directly to eligible farmer families via Direct Benefit Transfer. Free fertilizers is not the scheme's provision. Loan waivers are state-level decisions, not PM-KISAN. Free irrigation is handled by other schemes like PM-KUSUM.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Small and Marginal farmers constitute about 86% of all farmers in India.
Reason (R): The average landholding size in India has been declining due to successive fragmentation of agricultural land.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — about 86% of Indian farmers are small and marginal (holding less than 2 hectares). Reason (R) is correct — successive division of land among heirs has reduced average holdings. The Reason explains WHY so many farmers fall in the small/marginal category — continuous fragmentation keeps reducing farm sizes. Option B is wrong because (R) directly explains (A). Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which of the following is the apex institution for agricultural credit in India?
questions.explanation: NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) is the apex institution for agricultural and rural credit in India, refinancing lending institutions and promoting rural development. RBI is the central bank for overall monetary policy. SBI is a commercial bank. SIDBI (Small Industries Development Bank of India) focuses on small industries, not agriculture specifically.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Special Economic Zones (SEZs) in India:

(i) The SEZ Act was passed in 2005.
(ii) SEZs provide tax incentives and simplified procedures to attract investment.
(iii) SEZs aim to promote exports and generate employment.
(iv) All SEZs are owned and operated exclusively by the Central Government.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — the SEZ Act was enacted in 2005. Statement (ii) is correct — SEZs offer tax holidays, duty-free imports, and simplified compliance. Statement (iii) is correct — their objectives include export promotion and employment generation. Statement (iv) is incorrect — SEZs can be set up by private, public, or joint sector entities, not just the Central Government.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following organizations with their primary functions:

Column I:
(a) FCI
(b) ICAR
(c) APEDA
(d) MSME Ministry

Column II:
(i) Promotion of agricultural exports
(ii) Agricultural research and education
(iii) Procurement and distribution of food grains
(iv) Development of micro, small and medium enterprises

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: FCI (Food Corporation of India) handles procurement, storage and distribution of food grains (a-iii). ICAR (Indian Council of Agricultural Research) conducts agricultural research (b-ii). APEDA (Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority) promotes agricultural exports (c-i). MSME Ministry develops micro, small and medium enterprises (d-iv). Option B swaps FCI with ICAR. Option C mismatches ICAR with APEDA. Option D incorrectly places FCI with MSME.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan' (Self-Reliant India Mission) was announced in which year?
questions.explanation: Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan was announced on 12 May 2020 by PM Modi with a stimulus package of ₹20 lakh crore to make India self-reliant, especially in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic. 2019 was before COVID. 2021 is after the initial announcement. 2018 predates the concept.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are kharif crops in India?

(i) Rice
(ii) Wheat
(iii) Cotton
(iv) Maize

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Kharif crops are sown with the onset of monsoon (June-July) and harvested in autumn. Rice (i), Cotton (iii), and Maize (iv) are kharif crops. Wheat (ii) is a RABI crop, sown in winter (October-November) and harvested in spring (March-April). Options B and D incorrectly include wheat as kharif.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India adopted the policy of economic liberalization in 1991.
Reason (R): India faced a severe Balance of Payments crisis in 1991, nearly running out of foreign exchange reserves.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — India liberalized its economy in 1991 under PM Narasimha Rao and FM Manmohan Singh. Reason (R) is correct — India's forex reserves had dwindled to barely two weeks of imports, forcing the crisis. The BOP crisis was the direct trigger that compelled India to adopt liberalization, privatization, and globalization (LPG) reforms. Option B is wrong because (R) is the direct cause. Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The contribution of agriculture to India's GDP (as of recent estimates) is approximately:
questions.explanation: Agriculture contributes approximately 15-18% to India's GDP (varying slightly year to year). 35-40% was its contribution decades ago but has declined as services grew. 25-30% is higher than the current figure. 5-8% is too low — agriculture still plays a significant role. Despite low GDP share, agriculture employs about 42% of the workforce.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about MSME (Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises) in India:

(i) MSMEs contribute significantly to India's manufacturing output and employment.
(ii) The classification of MSMEs was revised in 2020 based on investment and turnover criteria.
(iii) MSMEs account for about 30% of India's GDP.
(iv) The Udyam Registration portal was launched for online MSME registration.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All statements are correct. MSMEs significantly contribute to manufacturing and employment (i). The revised classification (2020) uses both investment in plant/machinery AND annual turnover (ii). MSMEs contribute approximately 30% of GDP (iii). The Udyam Registration portal provides free, paperless online registration (iv).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The __________ is the principal crop insurance scheme in India that covers farmers against crop loss due to natural calamities.
questions.explanation: PMFBY (Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana) is India's principal crop insurance scheme, covering farmers against crop loss from natural calamities, pests, and diseases at low premium rates. PM-KISAN provides income support, not insurance. RKVY funds agricultural development projects. Soil Health Card tests soil quality — none of these provide crop insurance.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which Five-Year Plan in India gave highest priority to industrialization and the development of heavy industries?
questions.explanation: The Second Five-Year Plan (Mahalanobis Plan) prioritized rapid industrialization, especially heavy and basic industries like steel, machinery, and chemicals. The First Plan focused on agriculture and irrigation. The Third Plan continued industrialization but was disrupted by wars. The Fourth Plan focused on self-reliance and growth with stability.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following Indian public sector enterprises with their primary industries:

Column I:
(a) SAIL
(b) BHEL
(c) HAL
(d) ONGC

Column II:
(i) Oil and natural gas
(ii) Steel
(iii) Aerospace/Defence
(iv) Power equipment

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: SAIL (Steel Authority of India Limited) — steel (a-ii). BHEL (Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited) — power equipment (b-iv). HAL (Hindustan Aeronautics Limited) — aerospace/defence (c-iii). ONGC (Oil and Natural Gas Corporation) — oil and gas (d-i). Option B swaps SAIL with BHEL. Option C mixes BHEL with HAL. Option D incorrectly pairs SAIL with oil.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'e-NAM' (electronic National Agriculture Market) platform aims to:
options: Create a unified national market for agricultural commodities through online trading
Provide direct cash transfers to farmers
questions.correctAnswer: Create a unified national market for agricultural commodities through online trading
questions.explanation: e-NAM is an electronic trading portal connecting Agricultural Produce Market Committees (APMCs) across India to create a single national market for transparent price discovery and online trading. Cash transfers are handled by PM-KISAN. Import regulation is by DGFT. Free seed distribution is through state schemes, not e-NAM.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about India's textile industry:

(i) India is the world's second largest producer of textiles and garments.
(ii) The textile industry is one of the largest employers in India after agriculture.
(iii) India is the largest producer of jute in the world.
(iv) The textile industry contributes about 2% to India's GDP.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All statements are correct. India is the world's second largest textile producer after China (i). Textiles employ about 45 million directly plus 100 million indirectly, making it the second largest employer (ii). India is the largest jute producer globally (iii). The textile sector contributes about 2-2.3% to GDP (iv).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Soil Health Card Scheme' primarily provides farmers with:
options: Information about nutrient status of soil and recommendations for fertilizer use
Seeds suitable for their soil type
questions.correctAnswer: Information about nutrient status of soil and recommendations for fertilizer use
questions.explanation: The Soil Health Card Scheme (launched 2015) provides farmers with information about the nutrient status of their soil (N, P, K, organic carbon, etc.) and recommends appropriate doses of fertilizers. It does not provide free soil, financial compensation, or seeds — it is an advisory/diagnostic tool to help farmers use the right amount and type of fertilizers.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the sector-wise contribution to India's GDP:

Agriculture → 17%
Industry → 26%
Services → 57%

If India's total GDP is ₹300 lakh crore, what is the contribution of the Industry sector (in ₹ lakh crore)?
questions.explanation: Industry contribution = 26% of ₹300 lakh crore = 0.26 × 300 = ₹78 lakh crore. Option 51 = 17% of 300 (that's agriculture). Option 171 = 57% of 300 (that's services). Option 90 = 30% of 300 (incorrect percentage).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which of the following correctly describes 'Contract Farming'?
options: An agreement between farmers and buyers for production and supply of agricultural products at predetermined prices
Farming done exclusively on government-owned land
Farming by hired labourers without land ownership
Agriculture practised only for export purposes
questions.correctAnswer: An agreement between farmers and buyers for production and supply of agricultural products at predetermined prices
questions.explanation: Contract farming involves a pre-agreed contract between farmers and agri-business firms/buyers for production and purchase at set prices, reducing price risk for farmers. 'Farming on government land' describes government farms. 'Farming by hired labourers' is wage labour, not contract farming. 'Only for export' is too narrow and inaccurate.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India has become self-sufficient in food grain production since the Green Revolution.
Reason (R): The introduction of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilizers, and irrigation transformed Indian agriculture.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — India transformed from a food-deficit nation to self-sufficient (even exporting food grains). Reason (R) is correct — HYV seeds, fertilizers, pesticides, and irrigation were the key technological inputs of the Green Revolution. The Reason explains the mechanism by which India achieved food self-sufficiency. Option B is wrong because (R) explains (A). Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are challenges faced by Indian agriculture?

(i) Fragmentation of land holdings
(ii) Dependence on monsoon for irrigation
(iii) Inadequate cold storage and warehousing
(iv) Excessive mechanization in all regions

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Land fragmentation (i), monsoon dependence — about 52% of farmland is rain-fed (ii), and inadequate cold chain/storage leading to post-harvest losses (iii) are major challenges. Statement (iv) is incorrect — the challenge is INSUFFICIENT mechanization in many regions, especially in small and marginal farms, not excessive mechanization.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Startup India' initiative was launched in which year?
questions.explanation: Startup India was launched on 16 January 2016 to build a strong ecosystem for nurturing innovation and startups. 2014 saw Make in India. 2018 is too late. 2020 saw Atmanirbhar Bharat, not Startup India.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the production of food grains in India (in million tonnes):

2018-19 → 285
2019-20 → 297
2020-21 → 310
2021-22 → 315

What is the approximate percentage increase in food grain production from 2018-19 to 2021-22?
questions.explanation: Percentage increase = (315-285)/285 × 100 = 30/285 × 100 = 10.53% ≈ 10.5%. Option 15.2% would require an increase of about 43 MT. Option 8.3% would be 23.6 MT increase. Option 12.0% would be 34.2 MT increase. The actual increase of 30 MT corresponds to 10.5%.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The __________ was India's first steel plant set up in the public sector after independence, established with Soviet assistance.
questions.explanation: Bhilai Steel Plant in Chhattisgarh (then Madhya Pradesh) was established with Soviet/Russian assistance in the public sector during the Second Five-Year Plan. Tata Steel in Jamshedpur is a private sector company established in 1907, not public sector. Rourkela was established with German assistance. Durgapur was set up with British assistance. Among public sector plants with Soviet help, Bhilai is the correct answer.
